# Diagnose the competent bot's level-3 survival drift in the ring-timing arena

> Treats `discovered-from:AH-0MVWWGN92008P366` (producer ruling Q-A = (b): investigate the level-3 survival drift before re-deciding ring 2's budget window).

## Problem statement

The competent bot no longer reliably survives campaign level 3 in the ring-timing arena: the committed baseline (a7c57da1, 2026-11-03) captured every level-3 hex (aggression 2) at the full 300 s window on all three seeds, but today the same runs die at ~250–266 s of the 300 s window on 2 of 3 seeds. The drift must be bisected to its source commit and fixed so the ring-timing evidence is trustworthy again. This blocks `Restore ring 2's 70–100 window and regenerate the ring-timing evidence (AH-0MW9VARCU000XZIL)`: no aggression band the ring rules allow lands ring 2 in 70–100 while level 3 is borderline (maximal flattening to aggression 2 models 117.10 min). The window decision is deferred until this drift is explained and fixed.

## Impact

The ring-timing evidence is trustworthy again — level-3 hexes capture at the full window on all seeds — so ring 2's survivable aggression band can be re-decided from a baseline the producer can rely on.

## Users

- **The producer / ring-balance decision maker** — decides ring 2's aggression window (70–100) from the measured ring-timing budgets; needs trustworthy, reproducible arena evidence.
- **The balance-tuning developer** — owns `src/ai/eval/` and the ring-timing harness; needs the arena to measure the shipped weapons faithfully.
- **The bot-AI developer** — owns the competent bot's survival logic; needs to know whether the drift is a bot, weapon, or arena-fidelity problem.

**User stories:**

- As a producer, I want the ring-timing harness to reproduce the committed baseline so I can trust the budgets when re-deciding ring 2's window.
- As a balance developer, I want the arena's wave-laser model to match what ships in the game, so measured budgets do not silently depend on an outdated (travelling-bullet) approximation.
- As a developer inheriting this code, I want the drift's root cause recorded with a reproducible bisect, so a new balanced change cannot quietly re-introduce it.

## Evidence (measured today, harness untouched)

- Baseline a7c57da1 ring-1 grind: `hex-r1-1` / `hex-r1-4` (level 3) captured at 300 s in ALL seeds.
- Today: seed 1 -> 250.2 s (lost), seed 2 -> 300 s (captured), seed 3 -> 266.1 s (lost). Ring 2's six aggression-2 hexes mirror this exactly (they share the seed stream).
- Ring 2 grind regenerated total: **111.94 min (95.56–120.78)**, captured 2.67/12, `missed` against 70–100. Copy of the regenerated artifact held at `/tmp/ring-timing-baseline.retune-70-100.json`.

## Prime suspect — the wave-laser hitscan redesign (AH-0MVREBUJ5004HDRQ)

The wave-laser redesign (post-baseline, 2026-11-03 13:31) changed the weapon from a **pass-through beam with a damage budget** (`maxHitPoints`, lifetime 1.0) to a **single 1-damage hitscan ray that stops at the first enemy** (lifetime 0.3). The arena does **not** model the hitscan seam — `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` documents "the Wave Laser's hitscan ray and the Options pods' orbits (both fire as a travelling bullet)" — so in the arena the wave laser is now a plain 1-damage, short-reach, non-piercing bullet.

The ring-timing harness awards permanent weapon grants through the shared hold-full choice flow (`chooseOptions` in `src/powerups/choice.ts`; `wave_laser` is a levelable weapon drop), and the arena simulates the fire output of every owned grant from the shared `src/utils/weapons.ts` / `weaponLevels.ts`. A bot that takes a wave_laser grant mid-run therefore lost most of its crowd-control DPS on the day the redesign merged, which matches the timing of the baseline (10:30) vs. the redesign (13:31) both on 2026-11-03.

## Change window to bisect

a7c57da1..dev is 175 commits. Gameplay-relevant candidates besides the wave-laser redesign:

- `AH-0MVREBUJ5004HDRQ` wave-laser hitscan redesign — prime suspect.
- Weapon catalogue CSV codec + runtime invariant guards (AH-0MW0Q1DCZ006AUGP, AH-0MW0Q1FT1002Q6NJ) — could adjust weapon data.
- `Pin the boss-walk reward to a damage-neutral set` (AH-0MW3MLV2V001NWBR).
- `Halve bulletSpeed fallback from 200 to 100 in unknown-archetype paths` (AH-0MUX3VFUW009M539) — enemy bullet speed fallback (easier, not harder; but verify no path regressed).
- `Pin fixed-speed dive timing assertions` (AH-0MW3MWWOA009GRVM) — enemy dive timing.
- Mining-laser catalogue additions (AH-0MW9QMQ7B005WFH9 et al.) — new weapon in the drop/choice pool could change offer weights.

## Verification (bisect)

1. Reproduce: run `npm run ring-timing` on current dev; confirm ring-1 level-3 losses on seeds 1/3 (this item's evidence).
2. Checkout the arena+baseline state at a7c57da1 in a throwaway worktree and re-run the harness; expected: level-3 hexes captured at 300 s on all seeds (baseline numbers reproduce).
3. Bisect the gameplay commits between a7c57da1 and HEAD (start with the wave-laser redesign) by re-running the **ring-1 grind, seed 1** (`npm run ring-timing -- --ring 1 --strategy grind --seed 1`) at each candidate; the seed-1 level-3 death at 250.2 s is the discriminator.
4. Confirm the mechanism: patch the arena's weapon-fire model (or inspect a run's choice sequence) to show an owned wave_laser grant's DPS collapse as the trigger.

## Fix options (decide after the bisect; the fix is this item's deliverable)

- **(a) Arena fidelity fix:** model the wave-laser hitscan ray in the arena (the shared `src/vfx/hitscanBeam` seam) so the arena measures the shipped weapon, not a travelling-bullet approximation. Touches `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` + tests; re-baseline.
- **(b) Balance the arena's travelling-bullet representation** of the redesigned wave laser (e.g. fire-rate/level curve compensation) if (a) proves too invasive; re-baseline.
- **(c) If the bisect exonerates the wave laser, apply the same bisect to the other candidates** and fix the actual drift source found.

## Constraints

- The arena's documented fidelity boundary must be respected: any change to the "not modelled" list (hitscan seam) must update the `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` doc block and any mirror docs.
- The ring-2 window decision (70–100) is intentionally OUT of scope — it belongs to AH-0MW9VARCU000XZIL once the evidence is stable.
- Regenerated `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` is the committed evidence artifact; it must be regenerated from the fixed build, not hand-edited.
- Bisect work must happen in throwaway worktrees — never edit, commit, or push from the main checkout (worktree isolation requirement).
- No ad-hoc test runs: all test execution goes through the test skill (`/skill:test`).

## Existing state

The ring-timing arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) explicitly does not model the wave laser's hitscan ray (documented "not modelled" entry); `npm run ring-timing` on current `dev` reproduces the level-3 losses; committed baseline `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` (2026-11-03) predates the wave-laser redesign.

## Desired change

A bisected, mechanism-stated explanation of why the competent bot's level-3 survival collapsed, plus a fix (arena fidelity or compensated arena representation) that returns ring-1 measured captures to baseline behaviour on a regenerated, committed baseline — with the arena's documented fidelity boundary and tests kept consistent.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — arena weapon-fire model; documents the wave-laser hitscan seam as "not modelled"; primary fix target for option (a).
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts`, `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts` — arena/ring-timing tests; regression coverage for the fix.
- `src/ai/eval/ringTiming.ts` — pure ring-timing core driving the harness.
- `scripts/ring-timing.mjs` — harness CLI (`npm run ring-timing`).
- `src/vfx/hitscanBeam.ts` — the shipped hitscan beam seam (`spawnHitscanBeam`, lifetime 0.3) the arena would model under option (a).
- `src/utils/weapons.ts`, `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — shared weapon data the arena simulates fire output from.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — hold-full choice flow awarding `wave_laser` grants mid-run.
- `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` — committed baseline artifact to regenerate.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — ring-timing/balance documentation to keep consistent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The drift is reproduced and **bisected to a specific commit(s)** between a7c57da1 and HEAD, with the mechanism stated (which change degrades the bot's level-3 survival and how).
- The ring-1 grind measured captures return to the baseline behaviour (level-3 hexes captured at the full window on all seeds) — or a documented, deliberate deviation with a recorded reason.
- `docs/dev/ring-timing-baseline.json` is regenerated from the fixed build and both grind budgets are in-window against the currently committed 90–120 window while the ring-2 window decision is pending (this item does NOT re-decide the window — that is AH-0MW9VARCU000XZIL once the evidence is stable).
- The changed-scope test gate (`/skill:test`) passes.
- Findings (bisect result + mechanism) are recorded in this item's comments; the fix is linked to the drift commit found.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Bisect cost:** 175 commits in the window; each candidate re-run of the seed-1 ring-1 grind is a full harness evaluation, so worst-case bisect time is high. Mitigation: start with the prime suspect (wave-laser redesign) and stop at the first commit that reproduces the seed-1 death at ~250.2 s.
- **Suspect misidentification:** if the wave-laser bisect step does not reproduce, the arena may already be measuring a representative approximation and the true trigger may be elsewhere (e.g. offer-weight shifts from mining-laser catalogue additions). Mitigation: option (c) — continue the bisect across the other candidates rather than forcing option (a)/(b).
- **Arena-fidelity fix risk (a):** modelling the hitscan seam could make the arena strictly harder than the game or interact with the documented "not modelled" boundary — needs its own tests and could shift other weapons' measured budgets. Mitigation: keep the change surgical, update the `arena.ts` doc block, and re-baseline.
- **Confound from harness loadout (AH-0MW9QA2YC009PSF5):** if the harness plays a campaign-reset loadout instead of the deployment hangar loadout, survival numbers may differ independent of the wave laser. Mitigation: rule this out during reproduction (verification step 1) before bisecting.
- **Scope creep:** window re-decision (70–100) and related balance retunes are tracked by other items (AH-0MW9VARCU000XZIL et al.) and must not creep into this item. Assumption: the arena remains the reference for ring budgets; the game's real wave-laser behaviour is unchanged by this item.

## Related work

- `AH-0MW9VARCU000XZIL` — Restore ring 2's 70–100 window and regenerate the ring-timing evidence (blocked by this item).
- `AH-0MVWWGN92008P366` — Review ring 2 aggression floor against the measured builds/losses split (source producer ruling, `discovered-from`).
- `AH-0MVREBUJ5004HDRQ` — Wave laser redesign (prime suspect commit, completed).
- `AH-0MVUXCBQY001ESWT` — Ring timing validation and playstyle balance (harness origin, completed).
- `AH-0MW0N1UKU000I65T` — [test-failure] ringTiming.test.ts: the 12-hex ring 2 grind lands inside the 90–120-minute budget (failing test, completed) — gate lit by this drift.
- `AH-0MW9QA2YC009PSF5` — Ring-timing harness plays a campaign-reset loadout, not the deployment's hangar loadout (open — possible confound to rule out during reproduction).
- `AH-0MW0KSCU20096B02` — Derive the ring-timing docs guard's measured means from the committed baseline artifact (open, chore).
- `AH-0MW0UHYMQ003OS84` — README still describes the Wave Laser as a piercing budget beam (open, docs — mirrors the hitscan redesign).
- Automated related-work report: see `## Related work (automated report)` appended by the find-related skill.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MW9VARCU000XZIL** – Restore ring 2's 70–100 window and regenerate the ring-timing evidence (blocked)
- **AH-0MW0N1UKU000I65T** – [test-failure] src/ai/eval/ringTiming.test.ts > ring timing: real arena evidence > the 12-hex ring 2 grind lands inside the 90-120-minute budget — failing test (completed)
- **AH-0MVUXCBQY001ESWT** – Ring timing validation and playstyle balance (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0mvrebuj5004hdrq, 0mw3mlv2v001nwbr, acceptance, actual, adjust (+228 more)
- `README.md` — matched: 0mvrebuj5004hdrq, acceptance, actual, adjust, aggression (+220 more)
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: acceptance, allow, apply, approximation, archetype (+209 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which fix option (a/b/c) should this item commit to?" — Answer (producer, via ruling AH-0MVWWGN92008P366 Q-A = (b)): "Investigate the level-3 survival drift first; decide the fix after the bisect result." Source: work-item description (existing ACs). Research: the item's own fix-options section explicitly defers the choice until the bisect names the drift commit; asking up front would pre-empt that evidence. Final accepted answer: option choice stays open until the bisect completes (options (a)/(b)/(c) as written).
- Q: "Should the ring-2 70–100 window be re-decided here?" — Answer (existing content): "No — window re-decision is AH-0MW9VARCU000XZIL, deferred until the evidence is stable." Source: work-item description AC 3. Final accepted answer: out of scope, recorded as a constraint.
- No further clarifying questions required — the seed context (evidence, suspects, bisect plan, fix options, ACs) was sufficient to draft the brief; repo searches confirmed the referenced files (arena hitscan doc block, `src/vfx/hitscanBeam.ts`, harness, baseline artifact).

## Plan review note — additional bisect candidate (added during /skill:plan)

The candidate list above omits the arena's **own weapon-fire model**, which sits
inside the `a7c57da1..HEAD` window and is a stronger drift candidate than the
wave-laser redesign alone:

- **Baseline arena (`a7c57da1`)** fired a *fixed hardcoded cannon* only:
  `FIRE_INTERVAL_TICKS = 9` (≈6.67 shots/s at 60 fps), `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED = 420`,
  `PLAYER_BULLET_LIFETIME = 0.75`. It did **not** consume hold-choice weapon
  grants as fire output (`resolveWeaponLoadout` did not exist; `getWeaponLevels()`
  fed choice offers only). A `wave_laser` grant therefore had **no effect** on
  the committed baseline measurement.
- **Current arena** fires the shared-resolved cannon (`fireRateMs` 375 ms =
  ≈2.67 shots/s, `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED` 350, lifetime 0.75) **plus** every grant
  (AH-0MW5DV9I6001D4HN `ad017ee1`, 2026-11-07; AH-0MW5DVAME0062GQO `6ecbab23`,
  2026-11-07). The cannon alone therefore lost ≈60 % of its shots/s and ≈17 % of
  its reach relative to the baseline, while the added wave laser is a single
  1-damage, ≈105 px, non-piercing bolt (750 ms cadence).
- **Timeline correction:** the wave-laser redesign (`e1d8408d`, 2026-11-03
  13:31) *predates* the arena fire model, so the redesign by itself could not
  have changed the baseline measurement. The redesign reaches the arena only
  through the 2026-11-07 fire-model commits.

Bisect implication: include `ad017ee1`/`6ecbab23` (arena shared-resolver cannon
+ grants) as the **first** candidate after reproduction, and treat the
wave-laser redesign as a secondary mechanism — do not assume the wave laser
alone is the drift source.

Additional clarification (does not change the existing ACs): the bisect must
distinguish **"the arena is now more faithful to the shipped cannon"** (a
legitimate fidelity correction → documented deliberate deviation + re-baseline,
per AC 2's "or a documented, deliberate deviation") from **"a gameplay
regression"** (→ fix the regression). The fix decision (options a/b/c) follows
the bisect result, as already stated.
